name: Question 1
problem:
For the polynomial $f(x)=8{x}^{4}-2x+1,$ show that $f=O(1)$ as $x\to 0.$We say $f(x)$ is of order $g(x)$ as $x\to a,$ and we write 

$$
f(x)=O(g(x))\,\text{as}\,x\to a
$$

if there exist {{field-1}} constants $K$ and $\delta $ such that

$$
{{field-2}}\,\text{for all}\,0<|x-a|<\delta .
$$

So, in our case, we need to show that

$$
{{field-3}}\,\text{for}\,{{field-4}}.
$$

By the triangle inequality,

$$
\begin{aligned}|f(x)| & \le {{field-5}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

For the polynomial f(x)=8x4−2x+1, show that f=O(1) as x→0.We say f(x) is of order g(x) as x→a, and we write f(x)=O(g(x))asx→a if there exist
positive
positive
real
constants K and δ such that

|f(x)|≤K|g(x)|
|f(x)|≤K|g(x)|
f(x)≥Kg(x)
f(x)≤Kg(x)
|f(x)|≥K|g(x)|
{(|f(x)|≤K|g(x)|)(S1)}for all0<|x−a|<δ.

So, in our case, we need to show that

 
|f|≤Kx4
|f|≤K
|f|≤Kx
 
0<|x−1|<δ
0<|x|<δ
{(|f|≤Kx4)(S2)}for{(0<|x−1|<δ)(S3)}.

By the triangle inequality,

 
8|x|4+2|x|+1
|x|4+2|x|+1
8|x|4−2|x|
|f(x)|≤{(8|x|4+2|x|+1)(S4)}.
